summary: Hirofumi Isoda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University around 1963–1966. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (~1974–1999) and became professor emeritus at Shimane University.

Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He held posts as professor at Tokushima University (~1970–1999), special researcher at Rissho University, and professor at Soka University (~1999–2003).

Hirofusa Amano was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano. He held posts at Hijiyama University and Shimane University, where he became professor emeritus.

Hiroko Kawanami works in Buddhist and religious studies and studied under John Okell and Anna Allott. She became a senior lecturer at Lancaster University around 1995 and taught Kan Boonyakanchana and Jianchengshi.
Hiroko Matsuoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University. She held an academic post at Leipzig University.

Hiromasa Tosaki studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earning a PhD at Kyushu University (~1953–1966) and studying at Harvard (~1961–1963) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, among others. He was a professor at Kyushu University (~1967–1994).

Hiromi Habata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Freiburg by around 2004 and studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. She held a researcher position at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Hiromu Kitanishi (1925–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, having studied at Otani University (~1947–1950). He later served as a professor at Otani University (~1968–1980) and Bukkyo University (~1980–1996).
Hironori Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a PhD student at Bukkyo University until 2015. He also held an academic post at Bukkyo University.

Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who finished doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo by around 1965. He served as president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College and as a professor at Matsusaka University around 1982.
Hiroshi Aoyagi is a scholar of Japanology who studied at International Christian University. He held an academic post at Nanzan University.

Hiroshi Araki is a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Kyoto University by 2013. He held posts at Aichi Prefectural University (~1993–1999), Osaka University (~1999–2010), and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2010).

Hiroshi Kanno studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1984), working in Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as director at Soka University (2001) and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (2001–2009).

Hiroshi Kōzen (1936–2023) was a sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1954–1963). He held posts at Aichi University of Education (~1968–1973), Nagoya University (~1973–1981), Kyoto University (~1981–2000), and directed Kyoto National Museum (~2001–2005).

Hiroshi Marui, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at the Eastern Institute, Musashino University, and as associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1992–2018).
Hiroshi Maruyama is a scholar of Indology who has served as a professor at Osaka University and as leader of Ayurveda Kenkyūkai.
Hiroshi Nemoto works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed an MA at Hiroshima University by around 2001 and served there as a professor around 2008.
Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Madras (~1978–1984). He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University around 1989–2004.
Hirotomo Teranishi served as a director at Soka University, succeeding Hiroshi Kanno in 2009.

Hisao Inagaki (1929–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1949–1953) and the University of London (~1966–1968). He held a post at SOAS (1970) and served as professor at Ryukoku University (~1982–1998).
